source_title: Effect of kiwifruit consumption on sleep quality in adults with sleep problems
authors_or_body: Lin HH; Tsai PS; Fang SC; Liu JF
key_finding: Adults with sleep problems ate two kiwifruit one hour before bed for four weeks and reported improvements in several sleep measures.
supports_claims: Two kiwifruit one hour before bed may support sleep quality for some people as part of a bedtime routine.
limitations: Small sample; ages 20-55; not senior-specific; does not prove cure for insomnia.
contraindications_or_cautions: Do not frame as cure or medication replacement; use clinician caveat for persistent insomnia or serious sleep symptoms.

source_title: Behavioral and psychological treatments for chronic insomnia disorder in adults: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine clinical practice guideline
key_finding: Persistent insomnia should be handled with evidence-based behavioral treatment and clinician guidance.
supports_claims: Food routines do not replace medical sleep care for chronic insomnia or serious sleep symptoms.
limitations: Guideline is for chronic insomnia treatment, not kiwi or food-specific sleep routines.
contraindications_or_cautions: Use caveat for chronic insomnia, sleep apnea symptoms, restless legs, severe snoring, breathing pauses, or daytime sleepiness.

key_finding: Kiwifruit contains natural sugar, fiber, vitamin C, potassium, and other nutrients.
supports_claims: Kiwifruit can be described as a fruit with natural sugar, fiber, vitamin C, and potassium.
limitations: Exact nutrient amounts depend on serving size and database entry; check before quoting numbers.
contraindications_or_cautions: Caution for diabetes carbohydrate planning and kidney disease or potassium restriction.

source_title: Kiwifruit allergy across Europe: clinical manifestation and IgE recognition patterns
authors_or_body: Le TM; Bublin M; Breiteneder H; et al.
key_finding: Kiwifruit can trigger allergic reactions in susceptible people.
supports_claims: People with kiwi allergy or latex-fruit reactions should avoid kiwi unless cleared by a clinician.
limitations: Observational allergy research; not a general nutrition trial.
contraindications_or_cautions: Caveat required for known kiwi allergy, oral symptoms, swelling, or latex-fruit reactions.

authors_or_body: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute
key_finding: DASH emphasizes fruits, vegetables, whole grains, low-fat dairy, beans, nuts, and lower sodium to help blood pressure.
supports_claims: A DASH-style breakfast pattern can support blood pressure control.
limitations: Guideline supports dietary pattern, not a single breakfast cure.
contraindications_or_cautions: Caution for kidney disease, potassium restriction, diabetes, food allergies, swallowing difficulty, and medication-adjacent changes.

source_title: A Clinical Trial of the Effects of Dietary Patterns on Blood Pressure
authors_or_body: Appel LJ; Moore TJ; Obarzanek E; et al.
key_finding: The DASH dietary pattern lowered blood pressure compared with a control diet.
supports_claims: DASH-style eating has been shown to lower blood pressure.
limitations: Controlled feeding trial; not a breakfast-only intervention; not a medication replacement.
contraindications_or_cautions: Avoid telling viewers to stop or reduce blood-pressure medication.

source_title: Effects on Blood Pressure of Reduced Dietary Sodium and the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) Diet
authors_or_body: Sacks FM; Svetkey LP; Vollmer WM; et al.
key_finding: Lower sodium combined with DASH produced larger blood-pressure reductions than either strategy alone.
supports_claims: Lower sodium plus DASH can support stronger blood-pressure improvement than either approach alone.
limitations: Controlled feeding trial; not proof that one meal cures hypertension.
contraindications_or_cautions: Caution for medication users and people needing individualized sodium or potassium guidance.

source_title: The effect of oat beta-glucan on LDL-cholesterol, non-HDL-cholesterol and apoB for CVD risk reduction
authors_or_body: Ho HVT; Sievenpiper JL; Zurbau A; et al.
key_finding: Oat beta-glucan supports cardiovascular risk reduction through lipid effects.
supports_claims: Oats bring soluble fiber that supports cardiovascular risk factors.
limitations: Lipid-focused evidence; do not claim oats directly cure or rapidly lower blood pressure.
contraindications_or_cautions: Caution for portion planning in diabetes and swallowing/dental limitations when relevant.
